I have a problem with standard alarm apps; if I'm in the middle of something and they go off, I will dismiss them, finish what I was doing, then forget that the alarm had gone off. Yes, even if it only takes me a minute to finish what I was doing - because then something else will get my attention, then something else, and so on.

What's great about Due is that it gently nags me. It just politely goes "ping" then shuts up for a minute. Then it goes "ping" again, and I think "yeah, yeah, nearly done". Then it goes "ping" again, I finish up and there's my reminder on the lock screen. It doesn't buzz and jingle and beg for attention until I tell it to shut up, so I can ignore it until I'm ready.  And if I know I'm not going to be able to do the task for a while, it's blindingly quick to snooze it for a few minutes, hours or days.

I use this app dozens of times in a day. Very very useful.

I like this app.  It's elegant, uncluttered, and relatively easy to use.  An update to iOS 7 is badly needed.  I don't find Due as intuitive as some other reviewers suggest it is, but it's simple enough.  I wouldn't want to see much added to this app (as this would be detrimental). But I would like to see more options when repeating an event: for example I can't repeat an event every Wednesday to Friday (I'd have to create three reminders to do that); nor can I set an event to repeat on the first and third Sundays of every month (I don't think I can do that at all).  Also I'd like the ability to add a note for information I need to complete a task when reminded.  Add these two features and an update to iOS 7 and it'd be a five-start app.
